transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, hi. Thank you. Um, I suppose what finally made me come in is that my appetite has just been all over the place for months. I work as a healthcare social worker, so I'm usually the one lecturing my patients about maintaining their nutrition when they get discharged. Just the other day I had this sweet older gentleman who absolutely refused to eat anything but applesauce, and I spent an hour trying to explain the importance of protein to his daughter... but anyway, I've been having these stretches where I just skip dinner entirely, and I've been losing weight without even trying. 

Which, you know, normally people might be happy about, but it means none of my work pants fit right anymore. I actually had to go down to the mall on Sunday just to buy a new belt, and the parking there is an absolute nightmare right now with all the construction they're doing on the overpass. It took me twenty minutes just to find a spot near the department store entrance. But, um, yeah, where was I? Even on the nights I don't skip eating, I just end up standing in the kitchen picking at crackers or a handful of dry cereal. Cooking a whole meal for myself just feels completely pointless.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time lately?

Sad? Um, no, I wouldn't really say I've been feeling sad. Not down, exactly. I mean, my sister is the one who gets sad. She cries at literally everything, even those commercials on TV with the rescue dogs. 

Actually, my neighbor just adopted a rescue dog, this scruffy little terrier mix. It barks constantly whenever the mail carrier comes by. And our regular mail carrier, Gary, he just retired last month, which is a real shame because he never mixed up our mail with the house across the street like the new guy does. They had a little retirement party for him down at the main post office. He was on our route for fifteen years, always wore those postal shorts even when it was freezing out in January... 

But, um, I'm sorry, what was the question? Oh, right, feeling down. No, I haven't really noticed feeling like that.
Have you been enjoying things you usually like to do?

Well, um, I guess I still go through the motions. Like, I still go out and water my garden, and I still show up to my book club on Thursdays. We meet at the library downtown, the one with that beautiful old stained glass window in the reading room. They've been trying to raise money to restore it for years, and they finally got a grant from the historical society. My friend Brenda is on the board, and she was telling me the whole saga about finding the right artisan to match the original glass from the 1920s. They actually had to ship some pieces all the way from a studio in Germany, which got delayed in customs for a month... 

But anyway, yeah, I still go to book club. It's just... I don't know, it all feels so flat lately. Half the time I don't even finish the book, or I end up leaving early. Even the garden, I'll go out there and it just feels like a chore, so sometimes I don't even start.
How much weight have you lost over these months?

Oh, exactly how much? Um, I'm not entirely sure of the exact number. Like I mentioned, my appetite has just been all over the place for months now, so I'm just losing this weight without even trying. I'd guess maybe ten or fifteen pounds? 

I only really confirmed it when I finally stepped on our scale last week. We actually just had to buy a new scale because my husband dropped a heavy glass bottle of mouthwash on the old one and cracked the digital screen. It was one of those fancy smart scales that syncs to your phone, which honestly I always found a bit invasive anyway. Why does my phone need to know my weight, right? My niece works in data security and she's always warning us about privacy with those smart home devices. She actually just moved to Seattle for a new job at a tech startup, and she was telling me how they had to drive her car all the way across the country. They stopped at Mount Rushmore, which I've always wanted to see... 

But, um, what were we talking about? Oh, right, the weight. Yeah, it just sort of falls off because, like I said, I'll have these stretches where I skip dinner entirely, or I just stand around picking at crackers or dry cereal because the idea of actually cooking a meal for myself just feels completely pointless.
Have you been feeling anxious or worried about things lately?

Anxious? Um, well, I wouldn't say I'm anxious, really. I mean, my job at the hospital can be stressful, sure. Being a social worker, you see a lot of difficult situations, especially when we're trying to figure out discharge plans for older patients who don't have family nearby. 

Actually, we had this one patient last week, Mr. Henderson. His son lives all the way in Florida, down near Tampa, I think. Or maybe it was Clearwater? Somewhere on the Gulf Coast. Anyway, the son is a marine biologist, which sounds like such a fascinating job. He studies manatees, and he was telling me on the phone about how they migrate to the warm springs in the winter because they don't have enough body fat to stay warm in the ocean. It made me think of this documentary I saw on PBS a few months ago about the coral reefs dying off in Australia. The footage was just stunning, but so sad. My husband and I went snorkeling in Hawaii for our tenth anniversary, and the water was so clear... 

But, um, sorry, what did you ask me? Worried about things? No, I don't think I've been feeling particularly worried or anxious lately. Just, you know, everything else I mentioned.
Do you find that you're no longer taking pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy?

Well, um, didn't you just ask me that? Or maybe you asked it a little differently earlier. But I mean, yeah, like I was saying about the garden and the book club, it's just not the same. I guess I just don't get that spark from things anymore. 

Speaking of the book club, we're supposed to read this historical fiction novel next month about the French Revolution. I usually love historical fiction, especially anything set in Europe. My husband and I took a trip to Paris a few years ago, right before everything shut down for the pandemic. We stayed in this tiny little boutique hotel in the Marais district, and there was this bakery across the street that made the most incredible almond croissants. I can still smell them if I think about it. The baker was this older gentleman who didn't speak a word of English, but he was always so sweet and would give us extra pastries. My husband tried to use his high school French to thank him, and it was honestly so funny because he kept mixing up the words for 'thank you' and 'goodbye'... 

But, um, anyway, yeah. I just don't really feel much pleasure in doing things right now. Even the things I used to love. It's just all very flat.
How long have you been feeling like things are flat and you're not getting pleasure from activities you used to enjoy?

Um, well, it's been quite a while now. I'd say it really started right around the time the divorce was finalized, which was about a year and seven months ago. 

It's funny, you know, because the actual day the papers came through, it rained so hard. Just a complete downpour. I remember because I had parked my car down the street from the lawyer's office, under this massive oak tree, and I had to run back in the rain. I ruined my favorite pair of suede flats. They were these beautiful navy blue ones I bought on sale at Nordstrom's during their anniversary event. I always try to hit that sale early because they run out of my size so fast, I'm a narrow seven and a half, which is surprisingly hard to find. My sister has the same problem, but she lives in Chicago, so she usually ends up ordering online. She actually just renovated her kitchen and put in these gorgeous quartz countertops that look just like marble but are supposedly way easier to clean. I've always wanted a big island in the kitchen like she has, perfect for rolling out pie dough...

But, um, what was I saying? Oh, right, the timeline. Yeah, since the divorce was final, about a year and seven months ago. That's when everything just started feeling so... flat.
Have you been feeling empty or hopeless lately?

Empty or hopeless? Um, well, I don't know if I'd use those exact words. I mean, maybe? It's hard to describe. 

It kind of reminds me of this feeling I had when I was trying to pack up my old office at the clinic before I transferred to the hospital. I had accumulated so much stuff over the years, you know? Just boxes and boxes of files, but also all these little trinkets patients had given me. There was this one little ceramic owl that a woman made for me in her art therapy group. She was such a sweet lady, Mrs. Gable. She used to knit these tiny little hats for the premature babies in the NICU. I tried knitting once, actually. My grandmother taught me when I was about eight years old. We would sit on her porch in the summer, drinking iced tea with fresh mint from her garden. Her mint plant just took over the whole flower bed, it grew like a weed. I tried to grow mint in my apartment last year, but it got these little white aphids on it and just completely withered away. I think I overwatered it, or maybe it didn't get enough sun in that window...

Um, but what were you asking? Hopeless? I'm not really sure if I feel hopeless, honestly. I just haven't really thought about it in those terms.
Have you been feeling sad or depressed most days, even if it's just a little bit?

Sad or depressed most days? Um, I guess I haven't really noticed it being every day, or most days. I don't really know if I'd call it sad, either. 

It's sort of like... well, it's like when I was helping my niece pick out a dress for her prom last spring. We went to this huge bridal and formal wear shop downtown, the one with the big crystal chandeliers in the window. She tried on maybe fifteen different dresses. There was this one that was a really pretty sage green, which is her favorite color, but the cut was just all wrong. It had this weird ruffling on the shoulder that made her look like a linebacker. We ended up getting coffee afterward at this little cafe next door. They make their own syrups in-house, and I had this lavender vanilla latte that was just out of this world. I tried to recreate it at home, actually. I bought some culinary lavender online, but I think I steeped it too long because the syrup ended up tasting like soap. My ex-husband used to hate floral flavors in food. He always said it felt like he was eating potpourri. He was really picky about food in general, actually. He would only eat his steak if it was perfectly medium-rare, and if it was even slightly overcooked, he'd send it back...

But, um, anyway. Sad most days? I'm not sure. I just haven't really kept track of it like that.
Do you feel like you're just going through the motions of daily life without any real emotional investment?

Um, yeah, I think "going through the motions" is exactly it. I still try to do the things I used to love, like watering the garden or showing up to my book club, but... 

Well, the garden is a bit of a lost cause right now anyway. I tried planting those heirloom tomatoes this year, the purple Cherokee ones? I got the seedlings at this little farmer's market a few towns over. But the deer just completely decimated them. I told my neighbor I was going to put up a taller fence, maybe chicken wire, but she said they just jump right over anything under eight feet. Her husband actually built this elaborate netting system for their raised beds. He's a retired structural engineer, so he gets really into those kinds of projects. He spent like three weeks designing it on his iPad before he even went to Home Depot for the PVC pipes...

But, um, anyway, I still go out there to water what's left, but most of the time it just feels so flat. Same with book club. I'll show up, but it feels like I have no real investment in it, and I usually end up leaving early. Or lately, I just don't even start the book at all. Last month we were supposed to read that new historical fiction novel set in World War II Paris. I usually love those, because my grandfather was stationed in France. He brought back this beautiful brass compass that sits on my mantel now. I have to polish it every few months because it tarnishes so quickly. I use that Brasso cream, and it smells so awful, like pure ammonia. It always gives me a headache if I don't open the living room windows...

Um, wait, what were we talking about? Oh, going through the motions. Yeah, I just... I don't really feel it anymore. I just sort of do it, or I leave early.
Do you feel like you're actually sad, even if it's just a little, on most days?

Sad on most days? Um, I don't know, maybe? It's really hard to pinpoint. I don't think I'd call it sad, exactly. 

It reminds me of when I was trying to pick out a new paint color for the guest bedroom. The walls were this really stark, hospital-white, and I wanted something warmer, you know? So I went to Sherwin-Williams and brought home, gosh, maybe twenty different paint swatches. I was leaning toward this pale yellow, they called it "Buttercup" or something. But when I painted a little square on the wall, it looked completely different in the afternoon light. It looked almost neon. My sister told me I should just go with a neutral beige. She has her whole house painted beige, but she uses all these colorful throw pillows and rugs to brighten it up. She gets them from this little import shop downtown. The owner travels to Morocco a couple of times a year and brings back these gorgeous hand-woven textiles. I bought a scarf there once, a silk one, but I accidentally put it in the washing machine and it totally ruined the fringe...

Um, but sad? I don't know. I'm not really sure if I'd say I'm sad most days. I just haven't really thought of it like that.
Do you feel like you're sad or depressed, even if it's just a little bit, right now?

Right now? Um, I don't think so. Not sad, really. Just... I don't know. 

It's funny you ask about right now, because I was just sitting in the waiting room looking at that magazine on the end table. The one with the article about organizing your pantry? I've been meaning to do that for months. I have all these matching clear plastic bins I bought on sale at Target, but they're just sitting in the trunk of my car. I actually had to move them around yesterday because I went grocery shopping and bought way too many of those mandarin oranges. The ones that come in the little wooden crates? My niece loves them. She can eat like five in one sitting. I used to buy them at Costco, but the last time I went, the line for checkout was all the way back to the dairy section. I ended up just leaving my cart and walking out. I felt a little bad for the employees who had to put it all back, but I just couldn't stand there for an hour. My feet have been bothering me lately anyway. I think I need to get new inserts for my shoes. I read somewhere that you're supposed to replace them every six months, but I've had mine for over a year...

Wait, sorry, what did you ask me? Am I sad right now? Um, no, I don't think I'm sad right now. Just... here, I guess.
How long have you been feeling like you're just going through the motions of daily life?

Um, how long? Well, I guess it's been going on since the divorce was finalized. That was about a year and seven months ago, I think. 

It feels like a lifetime ago, honestly. We had to go through this whole mediation process, and we met at this lawyer's office downtown. The building was one of those old, historic ones with the original crown molding and these beautiful hardwood floors. They creaked every time you took a step. I remember the mediator had this massive mahogany desk, and on the corner of it, she had this little glass terrarium with succulents in it. I actually tried making one of those myself after I saw hers. I bought this geometric glass container online, and I got all the different layers—the pebbles, the charcoal, the potting soil. But I think I overwatered it, because they all started turning yellow and mushy at the base. My friend Sarah told me you're only supposed to mist them with a spray bottle, not actually pour water in. Sarah's really good with plants. She has this huge fiddle leaf fig in her living room that almost touches the ceiling. She even wipes down the leaves with a damp cloth every week so they stay shiny. I keep meaning to ask her if she uses some special kind of fertilizer...

Wait, sorry, what was I saying? Oh, right, the timeline. Yeah, about a year and seven months since the divorce was final. That's when I really noticed I was just... going through the motions.
Do you feel like you have been depressed most of the time since your divorce was finalized?

Depressed most of the time? Um... I don't know if I'd say depressed, exactly. Just... empty, maybe? Or tired. 

It's sort of like how I felt after I tried to organize that neighborhood garage sale last spring. I spent weeks putting up flyers on all the telephone poles. I even went to the local print shop to get them done on that bright neon pink paper so people driving by would actually notice them. The guy working there was so helpful, he showed me how to use the industrial paper cutter so the edges would be perfectly straight. He said he used to work at a big publishing house in New York before he moved back here to take care of his mom. She has some kind of joint issue, I think? Anyway, the morning of the sale, it completely poured. Just torrential rain. Everyone had to drag their tables back into their garages. My neighbor, Tom, he had all these vintage records he was trying to sell—mostly 70s rock, like Led Zeppelin and Fleetwood Mac. He ended up wrapping them all in these heavy-duty contractor trash bags so the sleeves wouldn't get ruined. He actually built this incredible custom shelving unit in his basement just for his vinyl collection. He used reclaimed wood from an old barn out past the county line. I always meant to ask him for the contractor's number, because the railing on my back deck has been wobbly since the winter...

Um, but what were we talking about? Oh, if I've been depressed most of the time. I'm really not sure. I haven't really thought of it as being depressed, just... not quite myself.
Do you feel like you've been having a depressed mood for most of the day, nearly every day, since your divorce was finalized?

Most of the day, nearly every day? Um... I don't really know. I haven't really kept track like that. It's just sort of a blur. 

Like the other day at work—I'm a social worker at the clinic across town—I was trying to help this older gentleman fill out his Medicare forms. He had this enormous binder full of medical records, all color-coded with those little sticky tabs. It reminded me of when I was in grad school and I tried to color-code all my research papers by subject. I used these bright highlighters, but they ended up bleeding through the pages of this really expensive textbook I rented. I had to pay the full replacement cost at the end of the semester, which was just ridiculous because the book was already falling apart when I got it. The binding was completely cracked down the middle. I tried fixing it with that heavy-duty clear packing tape, but it just made it worse. I actually need to buy more of that tape. I'm supposed to mail a care package to my nephew at college. He's a freshman this year, studying engineering or something like that. I bought him this huge box of those instant ramen noodles, the spicy chicken kind, because I know dining hall food gets old so fast. When I was in school, the dining hall had this soft-serve ice cream machine that was broken half the time. We used to have to...

Wait, sorry. What did you ask me? Oh, if I'm sad most of the day. I mean, I guess I just don't really know. I wouldn't say I'm keeping track of it like that.
Do you feel like you're depressed right now?

Right now? Um... I don't think so. I'm just sitting here, really. 

Actually, while I was waiting out in the lobby, I was looking at that big fish tank you guys have. It's really beautiful. It reminded me of this aquarium my younger brother had when we were kids. He won this little goldfish at the county fair—you know, the game where you toss the ping pong ball and try to land it in one of those little glass bowls? He carried it all the way home in a plastic bag on the bus. We didn't have a real tank yet, so my mom put it in this giant glass mixing bowl she usually used for potato salad. She makes the absolute best potato salad, by the way. She puts a little bit of sweet dill pickle relish in it, which sounds kind of weird, but it adds this perfect tanginess. She always brings it to the neighborhood block party over the summer. Last year, the block party got completely rained out, and everyone had to cram into the Johnsons' garage down the street. Mr. Johnson has this amazing collection of vintage license plates from all fifty states covering his garage walls. He said it took him twenty years to finally find the one from Hawaii. I think he said he found it at a flea market up near... 

Wait, I'm sorry. I'm rambling again. Did you ask how I'm feeling right now? Um, no, I don't think I feel depressed at this exact moment. Just... I don't know, a little distracted, I guess.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in activities that you used to find enjoyable?

Lost interest? I mean, I still go through the motions of things I used to really love. Like, I'll go out to water the garden, or I'll show up to my Wednesday book club. 

Actually, the last book club was at Susan's house over in that new subdivision by the old textile mill. They did such a beautiful job renovating that mill. They turned the bottom floor into this artisan bakery that sells these incredible lavender scones. I tried making scones once, years ago when I was in grad school, but I didn't know you were supposed to use freezing cold butter. You have to grate it in, otherwise the dough gets too warm and they just turn out like dense little hockey pucks. My roommate and I ended up throwing them out in the yard for the birds, but even the crows wouldn't touch them. Crows are actually incredibly smart, you know. I read this article in a magazine in my dentist's waiting room about how they can recognize individual human faces and even hold grudges. Imagine a bird holding a grudge against you! My neighbor has this bird feeder that's supposed to be entirely squirrel-proof, but the squirrels figured out how to hang upside down from the rain gutter just to shake the sunflower seeds loose onto the patio...

Um, wait, I'm doing it again. Sorry. You asked about my interests. So, yeah, I still go to book club or get the hose out for the garden, but... most of the time it just feels really flat. Like the joy is completely drained out of it. I usually just end up leaving book club early, or, with the garden, I just look at it and don't even start at all.
Do you feel like you're depressed most days?

Most days? I mean... I don't know if I'd say most days. It's hard to really pin down exactly how many days. 

It's like trying to remember how many times it rained last month, you know? Actually, speaking of rain, my basement flooded a little bit during that huge storm we had a couple weeks ago. The sump pump just completely gave out. I had to call this emergency plumber, and he showed up at two in the morning driving this bright yellow van. It looked exactly like a school bus. It reminded me of when I used to ride the bus to elementary school, and our driver, Mrs. Higgins, used to give us those little cinnamon hard candies on Fridays. I loved those candies, but they always made my tongue feel kind of raw if I ate too many. I tried to find them at the grocery store the other day when I was picking up coffee filters, but they didn't have them. They did have this massive display of those seasonal pumpkin spice things, though. It seems like they put pumpkin spice in absolutely everything now, even things that shouldn't have it, like hummus. Who wants pumpkin spice hummus? My coworker brought some into the break room at the clinic, and it just sat there in the fridge for a week until someone finally threw it out. The fridge at work is always such a mess anyway. People never put their names on their Tupperware, so you never know whose...

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, if I'm depressed most days. Um, I really couldn't tell you for sure. I haven't been keeping track of it day by day like that.
For how long have you felt like the joy is completely drained out of the things you usually enjoy?

How long? Um, well, I guess this whole feeling of just... nothingness with my hobbies, it started right around when the divorce was finalized. So that would be about a year and seven months ago. 

Actually, the day the papers were finalized, I remember I had to go straight from the courthouse back to the clinic because we had this massive staff meeting about the new electronic health record system. Those systems are always such a headache to learn. They sent this trainer down from corporate who kept using all these ridiculous buzzwords like "synergy" and "bandwidth." He was wearing this really loud tie with little golf clubs all over it. My ex-husband used to play golf every single Sunday. He'd leave the house at 6 AM and wouldn't be back until late afternoon. He always insisted on cleaning his clubs in the kitchen sink, which drove me absolutely crazy because he'd leave little clumps of grass and dirt near the drain. I tried buying him one of those special cleaning kits you attach to your golf bag, but he said he preferred doing it by hand. I ended up giving that kit to my nephew for his high school graduation. He didn't even play golf, but I figured maybe he'd start. Kids are so hard to buy gifts for these days. They just want gift cards or digital downloads. When I was a kid, getting a physical present wrapped in shiny paper was the best part of...

Oh, goodness. I'm so sorry. I completely lost my train of thought again. But yes, the divorce was a year and seven months ago, and that's when I really stopped enjoying things.
Do you feel like you've been in a depressed mood for at least two weeks?

Two weeks? I mean, I really couldn't say for sure. Like I said before, I haven't been keeping a calendar or anything. 

Calendars actually used to be something I was obsessed with. I had this beautiful Thomas Kinkade one hanging in the kitchen for years. Every month was a different little cottage with those glowing windows. It always made me think of this cabin my family rented up in the mountains when I was twelve. We went in late October, and the leaves were just spectacular—bright reds and oranges everywhere. We tried to go hiking, but my younger brother, Tommy, managed to step right into a yellow jacket nest on the trail. He was screaming bloody murder, and my dad had to scoop him up and literally run back to the car. We ended up spending the rest of the afternoon in this tiny rural emergency room. The nurse there gave Tommy a popsicle that turned his mouth completely blue. It was one of those cheap, artificial blue raspberry ones. You know, they say blue raspberry isn't even a real flavor in nature. It was just invented by candy companies in the fifties because they had too many red flavors like cherry and strawberry and needed something different for the blue food coloring. I think I read that on the back of a cereal box once. Or maybe it was a Snapple cap. Do they still put facts on Snapple caps? I haven't had one of those in ages. My favorite was the peach tea, but then they changed the recipe or something, and it just tasted too sweet...

Wait, sorry. I'm drifting again. Um, so, a depressed mood for two weeks... I really don't know. I just haven't been tracking it like that.
